newsitem.title: USA: Fluke says jury awards Talon $6.0 mln.
newsitem.headline: Fluke says jury awards Talon $6.0 mln.

text.p: Fluke Corp on Wednesday said a jury in Los Angeles has found Fluke acted improperly in a case stemming from patent litigation between Fluke and Talon Instruments, and the jury awarded Talon $6.0 million.

Fluke said it does not intend to charge earnings with the contingent liability because it believes the cost should be covered by insurance. Fluke's insurance company, however, has indicated it will contest coverage of the damages, Fluke said.
In a statement, Fluke said it believes the jury decision is wrong, and it will appeal.

The award stems from a patent infringement suit filed in 1988 by Fluke against Talon. In that suit, a federal court ruled Fluke's patent had not been infringed by Talon, but it said Fluke did have reasonable grounds to sue.
Talon, however, sued Fluke in 1993 for malicious prosecution alleging Fluke had no good reason to sue and did so only to damage a competitor.
Wednesday's jury decision awared Talon $2.0 million in general damages and $4.0 million in punitive damages.
